chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: Women musicians: Hightower, Butler and Sturdivant
summary: Blakeney remembers Alma Hightower's insistence on playing as written, Loretta Butler as a good pianist and Marian Sturdivant working often with them.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Around that time Mr. Blakeney, there were several really talented and unusual women musicians; Mrs. Alma Hightower (phonetic spelling) was one, who later became a teacher of some outstanding students; Mrs. Loretta Butler, who was also a dancing teacher; and Miss Fannie (?) Benjamin, who is yet with us and playing.
Tell us a little bit about Mrs. Hightower; you did work with her on occasion?
What do you remember most about her?
I remember she was very artistic and insisted on the musicians playing exactly as written.
She played several instruments. On the jobs that you worked with her, what instruments did she play?
She also played the drums and the trumpet, and several other instruments.
What about Mrs. Loretta Butler, who later became a dance teacher. She was on the scene then too.
Yes, I can remember her, as a very good pianist.
Was Mrs. Marian Sturdivant playing at this time, the wife of Mr. Sturdivant? Did she work much at this time?
Yes she did, she worked alot with us. She was very good too, a very good musician.
